Identity: the registered original is the Federal Register printing of Executive Order 10125 at 15 FR 2391 (govinfo text layer, grade original_representation_unverified), signed April 26, 1950; the source URL is the govinfo PDF of the April 28, 1950 issue. Inventory corrected: one operative clause, offsets 1449 to the end of the sentence barring changes in conditions, from the enacting words to the last operative sentence. The dossier's span (offsets 672 to 3814) began at the order's heading and ran past the order's end, which comes at the words 'out of which the said dispute arose.' followed by the President's signature, into an unrelated Department of Agriculture regulation (Part 517, fresh apple export program, F.R. Doc. 50-3600) and the heading of Title 7 Part 201 (Federal Seed Act). The heading and the three recitals before the enacting words contain no command. Text: The order recites that a dispute exists between the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company, a carrier, and certain of its employees represented by the Brotherhood of Railroad Trainmen, a labor organization. Acting under section 10 of the Railway Labor Act, as amended (45 U.S.C. 160), it creates a board of three members, to be appointed by the President, to investigate the dispute; it bars any board member from being pecuniarily or otherwise interested in any organization of railway employees or any carrier; it directs the board to report its findings to the President within thirty days from the date of the order; and, as provided by section 10, it bars the Chicago & Illinois Midland Railway Company or its employees from changing, except by agreement, the conditions out of which the dispute arose, from the date of the order until thirty days after the board has made its report to the President. Ending: Executive Order 12553 of February 25, 1986 (51 FR 7237, held govinfo text layer) has an enacting sentence reading, in part, "it is hereby ordered that the following Executive Orders, and" and, on the next line, "any amendments thereto, are revoked:" (the table row for 10125 describes creating an emergency board to investigate a railroad labor dispute). The enacting sentence has no effective-date wording and no exception or saving clause, so the first end is dated on signing, 1986-02-25 (a reading disclosed for the reviewer; the March 3, 1986 printing date is not used). Report: the held National Mediation Board copy of the board's report (jobs/source-ladder/output/texts/queue_EO_10125_Actual_report_date_of_the_board_created_by_EO_10125_Presidential_Emergency_Board_Rail_d68f78cdf2.txt, a held text lead and not an authenticated original) has a cover page dated May 19, 1950 and a letter of transmittal to the President, signed by the board's chairman and two members (the text layer garbles the month in the letter's date line), which submits the board's report. The report deadline and the section 10 standstill are spent facts and not ends under the owner ruling of 2026-10-21 (option C): taking May 19, 1950 as the date the board made its report, the order was functionally spent on May 19, 1950 and the thirty-day period after the report ran to June 18, 1950 (a computed date, thirty days after that cover or transmittal date, not a date shown in a source); the order stayed on the books until the express revocation. The dossier has no citable record covering the report's date line, so the report date is stated here and is not entered as a later event. Prior research: the packet reports no prior claim or review for this order. Searches: current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog, each marked complete in the packet with no coverage warning; they are the packet's machine searches.
